transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I came in today because... I just keep getting these awful, unwanted thoughts. I constantly worry that I’ve missed something critical. 

It could be a wrong number in a data release at work, or an unlocked back door at home, or... or even just a bill paid from the wrong account. And the thing is, even when I know I checked it, my mind just won't let go of the possibility that I’ve caused some kind of disaster. It's just becoming really overwhelming to deal with.
Do you find yourself doing anything over and over to try to make these thoughts go away or to prevent the disasters you worry about?

Yes, I do. To try and calm myself down, I... I end up reopening spreadsheets I've already closed. I'll reread my emails line by line, just to be absolutely sure. And with the house or the bills, I check the locks and the payment confirmations over and over again. I actually have to do it in a specific, set order until it finally feels, you know, safe to me. 

It takes up so much time that some nights I’m still sitting at my desk hours later, and I have absolutely nothing actually finished. I'm just stuck checking.
Are you checking things over and over because you think it will actually prevent something bad from happening, or is it more that it just helps you feel less anxious?

I think it's mostly just to calm myself down. Like I was just saying, reopening those spreadsheets, rereading emails line by line, or checking the locks and payment confirmations in that set order... I do it because the anxiety gets so bad, and I have to keep going until it finally feels 'safe' to me. 

I guess logically I know that checking a spreadsheet for the fifth time isn't actually preventing a disaster, but I just can't shake the worry until I do it. That's why I end up still sitting at my desk hours later with nothing actually finished. I'm just doing whatever I can to make that awful anxious feeling go away.
Do you have any habits or actions that you feel compelled to perform in a very specific way, beyond just the checking behaviors you've mentioned?

No, not really. It's... it's pretty much just the checking. I don't have any other rituals or, you know, specific habits like that. The checking the locks, the emails, the spreadsheets... that takes up so much of my time and energy, but I don't feel compelled to do anything else in a certain way. Just the checking.
Would you describe these unwanted thoughts as popping into your mind against your will?

Yes, exactly. They just pop into my head completely against my will. That's actually why I came in to see you. I keep getting these awful, unwanted thoughts that I've missed something critical. 

It could be a wrong number in a data release at work, or thinking I left the back door unlocked, or worrying I paid a bill from the wrong account. And the thing is, even when I know I already checked it, my mind just won't let go of the possibility that I've caused some kind of disaster. The thoughts just force their way in and stay there.
Do you find these unwanted thoughts to be very disturbing or upsetting to you?

Yes, they are very upsetting. Like I said, they're just awful. It's so disturbing to constantly feel like I've caused some kind of disaster. Even when I know I checked the data release or the back door or the bill payment, the thoughts just will not stop. It's incredibly distressing to live with that constant fear that I've missed something critical.
Do you ever feel compelled to perform physical actions in a specific way, like touching or tapping things, as part of your daily routine?

No, I don't do anything like that. Like I mentioned before, it's really just the checking for me. I don't feel the need to tap things or touch things in a certain way. It's just the constant need to go back and check the locks and my work.
Do your unwanted thoughts often involve things being symmetrical or exact in some way?

No, not really. It's not about things lining up perfectly or needing to be exactly symmetrical. Like I said, it's just that overwhelming feeling that I've made a mistake or missed something important, and I have to go back and check it. It's not about how things look.
Do you feel like the things you check need to be in a certain order or arrangement for you to feel safe?

Yes, I do. The checking itself has to be in a certain sequence. To calm myself down, I end up reopening spreadsheets, rereading my emails line by line, and checking the locks and payment confirmations over and over in a set order. I have to go through that exact routine until it finally feels safe to me. It takes up so much time... some nights I am still sitting at my desk hours later, just repeating the cycle, with nothing actually finished.
Do you feel like the things you check need to be not just in a certain order, but also perfectly accurate or exact in some way?

Not really, no. I mean... I work with numbers all day, so the spreadsheets obviously need to be correct for my job. But the urge to check isn't about needing things to feel perfectly exact or just right. 

It's really just driven by that terrible feeling that I've made a huge mistake somewhere. I'm just looking for errors to make sure nothing bad happens, not trying to make everything perfect. So, no, I wouldn't say it's about exactness.
Do you think that if you didn't perform your checking rituals, something bad would actually happen, or is it more about feeling comfortable and in control?

I'm... I'm not entirely sure, to be honest. I don't always know exactly what the bad thing would be. It's just this overwhelming dread that a massive mistake is sitting there, waiting to cause a huge problem at work or with my finances. 

If I don't go through my routine, that panic just takes over completely and I can't focus on anything else. So... I guess I don't know if it's about actually preventing a specific disaster, or if I'm just trying to get rid of that terrible feeling so I can finally breathe again. I just know the fear is so strong that I can't move on until I do it.
Do you believe that if you didn't check things in your specific routine, a specific bad thing would happen as a direct result?

No, not a specific thing. It's not a logical cause and effect where I think, "If I don't check these spreadsheets in this exact order, I'll get fired tomorrow." 

It's just... well, like I was just saying, it's a general, heavy dread. I can't really name the exact disaster that's going to happen. I just feel absolutely certain that if I don't finish the routine, some massive error will slip through and ruin everything. So, no, I don't have a specific bad event in mind that I think is directly caused by skipping the routine. It's just the fear itself that I can't shake.
Have these unwanted thoughts and checking behaviors been affecting your relationships with family and friends or your ability to work and perform daily tasks?

Yes, unfortunately, it really has. It’s affecting pretty much everything. 

At work, I’ve actually fallen behind on some major deadlines. I'll stay late at the office just reviewing things over and over, but because I'm stuck in that loop, I still don’t finish the actual work I need to get done. 

And socially... well, I've basically stopped doing the things I enjoy. I used to go to salsa nights, and I love kayaking, but I don't do either of those anymore. I just can't get away from the checking and reviewing in time to actually make it out of the house. It just eats up my whole evening. So, yes, it's definitely getting in the way of my life.
Do you feel like the things you check need to have a certain balance or order to them, beyond just being in a specific sequence?

No, I don't really think it's about balance or symmetry or anything like that. It's just about making sure the information is correct and that I haven't missed a catastrophic mistake. The order I check things in is just the routine I've developed to try and make sure I cover everything, but it's not because the numbers or the files need to look a certain way or feel balanced. It's strictly about finding the errors.
Do you feel like your checking behaviors help you regain a sense of control when you're feeling overwhelmed by these unwanted thoughts?

Yes, that's exactly what it is. When the dread gets too heavy, the only way I can calm myself down is by doing the checking. 

I'll end up reopening all the spreadsheets I just closed, and I reread my emails line by line. It's not just work, either—I check the locks on the doors, and I go over payment confirmations over and over again. I have to do it in a set order until it finally feels "safe." 

It does give me a temporary sense of control, but... well, like I said, some nights I'm still sitting at my desk hours later, doing all this checking, and I haven't actually finished anything. But in the moment, it's the only thing that makes the anxiety stop.
Do you believe your checking behaviors are primarily intended to prevent something bad from happening, or are they mainly to reduce your feelings of anxiety?

I think it's mostly to reduce the anxiety, honestly. Like I was just saying, I end up reopening the spreadsheets, rereading emails line by line, checking the door locks and payment confirmations over and over in a set order... all of that is really just to calm myself down. I keep doing it until it finally feels safe. 

I guess I'm not always picturing a specific bad thing happening in those moments, I just can't stand the dread, so I have to check. And that's why, you know, some nights I’m still sitting at my desk hours later with absolutely nothing actually finished. I'm just trying to get rid of that feeling.
Do you feel like the things you check need to be perfect or flawless in any way?

No, I wouldn't say they need to be perfect. It's not about perfection or making something flawless. It's really just about making sure there isn't a massive error that's going to ruin everything. I just need to know it's not wrong, if that makes sense. I'm not trying to make it perfect, I'm just trying to make sure it's not a disaster.
Do you feel like the act of checking itself has to be done in a very precise or symmetrical way to feel right?

Yes, it does need to be precise. I think that's what I meant earlier when I mentioned doing things in a set order. It's not really about symmetry for me, but the sequence itself has to be exact. 

Like I was saying, to calm myself down, I end up reopening the spreadsheets, rereading the emails line by line, checking the locks and the payment confirmations over and over... and it has to follow that specific routine. If I mess up the order or skip a step, it doesn't feel "safe," so I have to do it again. That strict routine, that need to do it precisely the right way, is exactly why some nights I'm still sitting at my desk hours later with absolutely nothing actually finished.
Do you feel like the act of checking has to be done in a way that feels 'just right' to you, beyond just being precise?

I don't think so, no. I mean, I'm not really sure what you mean by 'just right' other than doing the sequence correctly. Like I said, it just has to be done in that exact order for me to feel safe and make the dread go away. It's not like a special feeling I'm looking for, just... finishing the routine so I can finally stop.
Do you feel like the act of checking has to be done in a way that feels symmetrical or balanced to you?

No, not at all. Like I think I mentioned a minute ago, it's really not about symmetry for me. I don't need things to look balanced or... equal on both sides, or anything like that. It's strictly about the sequence. As long as I go through the steps in the exact order I'm supposed to, that's what counts. So, no, balance doesn't really factor into it.
